label: August 3–9
title: “Thou Art Come … for Such a Time as This” —  Esther

items.text: What may appear to be random chance is, in fact, overseen by a loving Father in Heaven. The Lord is in the small details of our lives. He can guide our path and prepare us for such a time when we can be instruments in His hands to fulfill His purposes.

Each of us stands at a unique place and has an important task that only we can perform. The Lord gave you your responsibilities for a reason. There may be people and hearts only you can reach and touch. Perhaps no one else could do it in quite the same way.

Our intent ought not to be ‘What do I tell them?’ Instead, the questions to ask ourselves are ‘What can I invite them to do? What inspired questions can I ask that, if they are willing to respond, will begin to invite the Holy Ghost into their lives?’

The Lord can guide our path and prepare us 'for such a time as this' (Esther 4:14) when we can be instruments in His hands to fulfill His purposes. We might not always recognize the Lord’s influence in these 'small details' of our lives.

As you look for ways the Lord made it possible for Esther to save the Jews, ponder how He has given you opportunities to bless others. What circumstances or relationships has He guided you to 'for such a time as this'?

In the book of Esther, we learn from the faithfulness of Esther and Mordecai, but we also learn from the pride and anger of Haman. His feelings, words, and actions reveal his motivations and the consequences he faced.

Pride and anger can lead to downfall. Reading about Haman may prompt you to evaluate what motivates your feelings and actions. Are you inspired to make any changes? How can you turn to Heavenly Father for help?

Fasting shows that I trust and rely on the Lord. Notice why Esther and the rest of the Jews decided to fast. Consider how you can make fasting a greater blessing in your life and understand why the Lord asks us to fast.

When Mordecai and Esther stood up for their beliefs and their people, it often required great courage. Doing the right thing, especially when facing opposition or difficult circumstances, can be a powerful testament of faith.

The events in the book of Esther, though seemingly coincidental, were part of a divine plan. The Lord orchestrated circumstances to prepare individuals like Esther to be instruments in His hands for His purposes.
